messages:
maria: paging — seeing a sharp jump in short-request latency on prod inference (p95 ~800ms, normally ~120ms). Batch queue depth for serve-cluster-a is increasing, continuous-batcher backlog at ~4200 requests. Not a code deploy. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/serve-batches?orgId=1

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2467123456 — high inference latency on prod. Paging eng-oncall.

kevin: looking at traces — looks like small requests are being buffered too long waiting for batch fill. Throughput is fine, but latency penalty high. Batcher batch_size distribution shifted right (more small tokens waiting).

jess: any hot customer? can we throttle noisy tenants while we mitigate?

maria: top noisy tenants (by queued reqs): AcmeCorp (21%), Ledgerly (13%), internal-loadtests (9%). Acme is real production traffic (SLA customer).

kevin: my proposal: temporarily increase continuous_batch_wait_ms from 10 -> 40 ms and bump max_batch_size 64 -> 128 on serve-cluster-a only. That should let more small requests be coalesced so we trade a bit of p95 for overall throughput. Also put per-tenant soft-rate-limit for internal-loadtests and non-prod tokens.

jess: +1 for tenant rate-limits. We should avoid any global disable. Are we comfortable with p99 implications for Acme? Maria, do they have strict latency SLO?

maria: Acme has 200ms p95 SLO historically, but we already breached. I'll loop in CSE after immediate mitigation. For now prefer batch parameter tweak to reduce queue depth quickly.

kevin: executing change via control plane patch. Command I will run (cluster-scoped):

```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime-config/serve-cluster-a \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batch_wait_ms": 40, "max_batch_size": 128}'
```

This is reversible. If we see p99 blow up, we'll rollback to 10/64.

deploy-bot: config-patch accepted for serve-cluster-a. Change id: cfg-2467123456-1. Rolling to 10 nodes, start draining new config now.

kevin: also applying tenant soft-quota for internal-loadtests and Ledgerly to cap concurrent requests. Command:

```
opsctl quota set --tenant internal-loadtests --rps 50
opsctl quota set --tenant ledgerly --rps 500
```

ops-bot: quotas applied: internal-loadtests=50rps, ledgerly=500rps.

maria: after change, queue depth falling from 4200 -> 900 in 90s. p95 improved to ~300ms. p50 unchanged. Looks promising.

jess: any sign of errors or model OOMs with larger batches?

kevin: no OOMs. GPU utilization rose ~6%. KV cache hit rates stable. No model errors in logs.

maria: I'll open a quick incident note with timeline and customer impact for CSE: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2467123456

samir: taking handoff in 30m. Plan for next shift: keep batch_wait at 40 for next 15-30m, monitor p99 and Acme traces, begin gradual ramp-down of internal-loadtests quota and remove non-prod tokens from production if backlog fully cleared. If p99 > 2s for Acme, rollback to previous config and initiate fallback routing to smaller-capacity dedicated nodes.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: samir will be primary oncall at 2467123600. Add :eyes: to channel if you see regressions.

maria: note for handoff — don't change both wait_ms and max_batch_size concurrently again without staged canary. Did it here because situation urgent. Add a canary step next time: patch 1 node, observe 60s, then scale to cluster.

kevin: agreed. I'll create a small script for staged rollout and a dashboard panel that shows batch fill rate and small-request latency.

jess: also recommend adding a per-route bias to prefer immediate dispatch for labeled low-latency customers next iteration, so we can avoid impacting high-SLA tenants during global batch config changes.

samir: copying plan into my notes. I'll watch for 30m, then either start ramping down wait_ms (40->25->10) or keep stable if backlog reappears. If noisy tenant returns, will escalate to rate-limit their API key and reach CSE.

maria: thanks everyone. marking incident "mitigated" for now, but will keep this thread open for handoff and postmortem details.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2467123456 status: mitigated by eng-oncall. Awaiting postmortem.

samir: oncall ack, will follow up with postmortem draft and action items (staged rollout script, tenant-level traffic shaping guide, and dashboard).
